QUANTUM OPERATIONS WITH AN ACTIVE SOURCE: THE NEXT PHYSICAL OPENING
Astra research continuation, 31 October 2026

Selected result: a complete singlet/triplet measurement-and-return mechanism
from spin-independent electronic hopping, electrostatic controls, a prepared
Coulomb charge probe, and particle reservoirs. The barrier source can remain
unprepared and dynamically noncommuting. The proof retains both doubled-charge
states, every detector history, physical return, loading and elapsed time.

Status: derived and checked in an explicit orbital-mode interaction model.
This is not an experimental qualification, a fault-tolerance threshold, a
claim of historical priority, or a practical advantage over the same resources
used by an informed conventional controller. The original readout theorem,
active-source dark-gate theorem, local/pair controls, real compiler, optical
closure calculations and earlier counterexamples are preserved unchanged.

1. THE QUESTION I CHOSE

Can the physical algebra of ordinary interactions enforce a useful quantum
instrument even when its tunnelling amplitude is a noncommuting quantum
operator whose state and time dependence are unknown?

I selected a nondestructive two-spin singlet/triplet instrument as the
consumer. Complete success is consequential because this single pair
instrument, a supplied mixed-spin ensemble, classical feedback and pair
selection already suffice for universal quantum computation [R1]. The
universality theorem is established prior work. The present task is earning
its physical instrument, return and resource interface under the active-source
contract, rather than assuming an ideal spin projector or a pair-star gate.

There is a useful obstruction behind this choice. On a two-electron,
two-orbital system, all spin-independent controls act identically on the three
triplet orientations. That protects them, but also forbids a nontrivial gate
within that single triplet. Changing which PAIR is measured in a larger
register supplies noncommuting operations on the register's representation
multiplicities. This changes the required physical control bank.

AN EXPLICIT CHARGE OUTLET FOR THE ACTIVE-SOURCE HUBBARD INSTRUMENT
Working derivation, 31 October 2026. Root synthesis; not a qualified device.

1. Purpose and the resource boundary

The data comprise two electrons in two loaded spatial orbitals. Their spins
need not be polarized. A retained barrier source E is arbitrary, can be
correlated with the data/reference, and is never reset. Ordinary spin-independent
tunnelling has a Hermitian amplitude G_E with g I <= G_E <= h I. Source dynamics
can fail to commute with G_E. A charge readout is needed after each short tunnel
pulse; resolving BOTH doubly occupied states is essential to reliable return.

Here is a bounded microscopic-mode detector, using density-density Coulomb
coupling, single-particle helper controls, and particle outlets. It avoids
postulating a singlet projector as a detector coupling. Its fresh probe ORBITAL
state, calibrated controls, separate reservoirs and port discrimination are
explicit resources. This does not assert that every auxiliary is unprepared.

The underlying joint mode Hamiltonian contains only one-body hopping,
spin-independent density interactions, source-modulated data hopping, and
helper-to-lead tunnelling. No data pair-star or native spin gate is assumed.
Continuum, orbital and spin-breaking corrections are addressed in section 7.

spatial modes, p=0,1, with n_p1=n and n_p0=1-n. Probe spin is a spectator and
may be mixed. Assume no particle exchange between the data and probe wells.
The diagonal density part of the direct electrostatic interaction is

HUBBARD CAPTURE, CHARGE MEASUREMENT, AND RETURN WITH AN ACTIVE BARRIER SOURCE
Research contribution for Astra; 2026-10-31. Proofs below are new derivations in this work, not claims of priority. Hardware and STP computational universality are established prior art. This note does not claim a demonstrated device window or fault-tolerant architecture.

1. Consequence and change of consumer

The relevant physical consequence need not be a continuously moving dark-space gate. A complete, nondestructive two-spin singlet/triplet (STP) instrument, including return of the singlet branch to two singly occupied sites, is already a universal computational primitive when combined with supplied maximally mixed spins, classical feed-forward, and pair selection. Rudolph and Virmani proved this universality. Their polynomial construction is not an efficient fault-tolerant architecture; its state preparation and routing costs must be counted.

Here ordinary spin-independent hopping supplies the common quantum coupling by fermionic algebra. Full charge measurement supplies the irreversible outlet. Classical electrostatic detuning and barrier controls select edges and resonance. The source of the hopping can remain in an arbitrary state and evolve noncommutatively throughout. No local spin rotations, calibrated exchange pulse area, or postulated two-register holonomic star are used in the construction.

The essential correction is to retain BOTH doubly occupied charge states. A symmetric three-level Hubbard problem has a dark charge combination. A naive capture-and-continuous-return construction can trap that combination. Complete charge readout between bounded tunnelling pulses removes this obstruction, and yields a uniform success probability on every actual history.

2. Actual two-site Hamiltonian and its exact single-orbital reduction

There are two electrons in two spin-degenerate orbitals L and R. For sigma=up,down, the ordinary second-quantized Hamiltonian is

   + sum_sigma [c_R,sigma^dagger c_L,sigma + c_L,sigma^dagger c_R,sigma] x G(t)
   + charge-diagonal source shifts.
